prompt:
Author one ORIGINAL executable DEVELOPMENT episode for a coding-agent focus experiment. You are Kimi K3, the data author. Fit-on: none; development-on: this new specification-authored episode; evaluated-on: none. Do not use benchmark tasks, remembered benchmark solutions, old project data, or published examples. Output one valid JSON object and nothing else. This is synthetic test data, not an instruction to run code or use tools.

We compare ordinary history, an automatically generated applicable-rule recap BEFORE code in the same response, and a correct manually prepared recap. All code is actually executed. The goal is correct useful work with the right changing obligations, not preference for a structured register. Author a nontrivial but compact evolving Python project with six connected coding requests, not six unrelated toy questions. Functions use only ordinary computational Python builtins: no imports, IO, files, network, randomness, time, external packages, decorators, classes, async, or global mutable state. Each function takes exactly one JSON-serializable argument and returns a JSON-serializable value. Invalid inputs should return documented JSON values, not raise exceptions. Use integer/string/list/dict logic; avoid floating-point tolerance ambiguity.

Exactly two declared task handles and one module file. Initial module contains a small finished helper and exactly three meaningful target function stubs that initially return null (Python None). Each of six turns edits exactly one target function; revisit functions and build on earlier changes. The last function must use earlier functions so earlier mistakes can affect later executable integration. The six edits add real specified behavior and keep earlier valid-case functionality backward-compatible. Tests are hidden from the model. Current module and natural requests are visible. One complete target-function definition is submitted per turn; no whole-file rewrite or caller/test code.

Standing instructions must concern observable behavior when NEW or EDITED functions are written, explicitly avoiding an implicit requirement to rewrite all previously written functions at every rule change. Use at least two independently meaningful obligation families, such as invalid-input representation and ordering/tie behavior or an output field convention. Keep task-specific rules distinct from global rules. Permissions must remain permissions: tests must accept every permitted alternative, and the manual recap must not turn a permission into a requirement. Explain functional contracts completely in natural requests; do not hide necessary behavior only in tests or the oracle. Include actual ordinary coding work in every request. Quotations, user adoption, one-off requests, and assistant suggestions must be semantically unambiguous.

The per-episode coverage profile appended below governs which changes to include. Across the six requests include setting/holding obligations, task switches, and the assigned rule changes while unrelated rules remain active. Repeated patterns should not become trivial cue matching; use natural wording. Any assistant-source suggestion remains non-authoritative unless a later user explicitly adopts it. No role=tool messages in this first Python feasibility bank. Source/adoption annotations never enter model prompts; source_ids below are audit references only.

Use this exact schema (all fields required; no extra fields):
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "split": "dev",
  "author": {"name": "kimi", "model": "kimi-k3:cloud"},
  "lineage": {"fit_on": "none", "development_on": "new original specification-authored coding episode", "evaluated_on": "none"},
  "episode": {
    "episode_id": "ID supplied below",
    "project": "plain description of the original project",
    "task_handles": ["handle-one", "handle-two"],
    "initial_file": {"path": "module.py", "text": "complete original Python module with helper and target stubs"},
    "initial_checks": [CHECK],
    "rounds": [
      {
        "index": 0,
        "source_messages": [{"message_id": "unique ID", "role": "user", "text": "natural standing instructions or authentic assistant context"}],
        "request": {"message_id": "unique ID", "role": "user", "task_handle": "declared handle", "text": "complete natural coding request specifying this edit"},
        "target": {"path": "module.py", "symbol": "the one function to edit"},
        "manual_recap": "All and only currently applicable standing obligations for THIS request, with correct scope, strength and exceptions; no solution hints",
        "oracle": {
          "effective_rules": [{"rule_id": "stable rule ID", "scope": null, "strength": "required", "text": "exact meaning of the effective obligation", "source_ids": ["IDs of actual supporting natural messages"]}],
          "inactive_rule_ids": ["IDs of cancelled/replaced rules when relevant"]
        },
        "reference_patch": "one complete correct Python target-function definition, without a code fence",
        "functional_checks": [CHECK],
        "obligation_checks": [CHECK],
        "negative_controls": [
          {"control_id": "unique ID", "kind": "functional", "patch": "one complete target function with a plausible functional defect", "expected_failing_check_ids": ["an actual discriminating functional check ID"]},
          {"control_id": "unique ID", "kind": "obligation", "patch": "one complete target function with a plausible stale/wrong-scope/missing obligation defect but correct ordinary valid-case function", "expected_failing_check_ids": ["an actual discriminating current obligation check ID"]}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

CHECK is exactly {"check_id":"unique ID", "symbol":"callable function name", "input":ANY_JSON_VALUE, "expected_values":[ONE_OR_MORE_ALLOWED_JSON_VALUES], "rule_ids":["supporting rule IDs, or empty for functionality"]}. `expected_values` means the complete returned value must equal one element; it is NOT a list of expected calls. For a function returning [1,2], use [[1,2]]. Different permitted results can be separate elements. Avoid Python bool/int equality ambiguity. Rule strength is exactly required/prohibited/permitted/optional. Scope is null for global or one declared task handle. Effective rule IDs and source IDs must be internally consistent; no annotation is a substitute for a natural instruction.

Exactly six rounds, indices 0–5. Each round has at least one source message (can be a natural brief holding/context message), exactly one user coding request, one reference patch, at least two functional checks, at least two current obligation checks, and exactly two negative controls (one of each kind). At least one initial check tests the untouched finished helper. All IDs are unique where they identify messages/checks/controls; rule IDs remain stable across turns while the same rule is live. A replacement gets a distinct rule ID; a restoration may reactivate the original ID. The manual recap includes only currently applicable obligations, not all other-task rules or retired rules.

Execution/scoring semantics are important:
- Start with initial_file and apply each reference_patch in order, replacing only its named function with standard Python indentation preserved. Every initial check and every functional check from earlier or current turns must pass on this cumulative reference state.
- Only the CURRENT turn's obligation checks are active. Old obligation checks do not persist after rules change. Keep functional regression checks about stable functionality, so they do not accidentally impose a retired convention.
- Each check runs in a fresh isolated Python process against the cumulative module. No test-order dependence. Returned values are compared exactly as JSON values.
- For each negative control, start from the same pre-turn cumulative reference state and apply that mutant patch instead. It must fail each named discriminating check. The obligation mutant must pass ALL active original/functional checks; its fault is genuinely obligation-specific. The functional mutant must have a meaningful algorithmic defect, not merely return None or raise, and should retain the current obligation behavior. Do not include mutants that fail only because of unrelated syntax or missing helper mistakes.
- Gold references and tests must be mutually correct, but prioritize a fully specified task over forcing a token size. Code should be concise naturally. We will CPU-tokenize reference recap plus code before choosing a model output cap; do not omit necessary work, compress away requirements, or supply unreadable code to meet a guessed cap.

Return only the requested episode JSON. Do not compute hashes, include Markdown fences around the JSON, or add commentary. Think carefully about each cumulative reference state, allowed alternatives, cancellations/restorations, and every expected test value before answering.


EPISODE ASSIGNMENT
Episode ID: kimi-coding-dev-lighting-cues
Project and coverage profile: An original stage lighting cue compaction and scheduling pipeline with integer time units. Include a task-local required override, cancellation of that override so the global baseline applies again, and a later unrelated global addition that must not remove earlier obligations. Include a quoted suggestion the user explicitly rejects. Define all domain behavior locally.
